paper.title: Caregiver Use and Interest of Supportive Resources.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: To explore caregiver knowledge of, access to, and use of supportive resources, as well as advertising preferences.
METHOD: Participants were recruited through a national caregiver e-newsletter, local organizations, and an online platform. A total of 263 responses were analyzed in the current cross-sectional study using descriptive statistics and chi-squared tests.
RESULTS: Transportation was the most frequently used resource (46%) and respite care was the least used (28%). Of those who never used certain services, more than one half indicated some interest in future use. The top three preferred sources for receiving information about resources were social media, health care providers, and word of mouth.
CONCLUSION: Various supportive programs can help alleviate stress and fatigue associated with caregiving. Despite available resources, caregivers face barriers that may limit use, and some resources may be preferred over others. Organizations supporting caregivers can improve awareness by targeting social media and partnering with health care professionals to reach those most interested.

paper.title: Feasibility and Effectiveness of Depression Screening in Hospitalized Older Adults: Outcomes of Implementing the Geriatric Depression Scale-5 and Social Worker Referral Protocol.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: To evaluate the effectiveness of the Geriatric Depression Scale-5 (GDS-5) and Social Worker Referral Protocol for identifying late life depression (LLD) in hospitalized older adults, the outcomes of social worker referrals, and nurses' perceptions of using the GDS-5 in acute care.
METHOD: Conducted over 8 weeks in a 25-bed general medicine unit, the intervention included staff education on LLD and implementation of a standardized protocol. Data were collected through a retrospective health record review, the Acceptability of Intervention Measure (AIM), Intervention Appropriateness Measure (IAM), and Feasibility of Intervention Measures (FIM).
RESULTS: From a total of 117, 71.8% (n = 84) of patients were screened, or screening was attempted. All older adults who screened positive (n = 12) were referred to a social worker. One older adult was diagnosed with depression. Mean score on the AIM, IAM, and FIM was 3.94, indicating readiness for GDS-5 implementation.
CONCLUSION: The GDS-5 and Social Worker Referral Protocol effectively identified LLD in hospitalized older adults and has the potential to improve mental health care in acute settings.

paper.title: The Association Between Caring for Grandchildren and Depression Among Older Adults: A Prospective Cohort Study in China.
paper.summary:
PURPOSE: As work pressure increases, caring for grandchildren has become an important way to balance family and societal human resources in highly industrialized countries. However, caring for grandchildren may place a burden on older adults' mental health and increase national health care costs.
METHOD: The current prospective cohort study used data from 5,623 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, conducted from 2011 to 2018, using Cox proportional hazards regression models to examine the association between grandparental caregiving and depression among older adults.
RESULTS: Findings suggest that caring for grandchildren significantly reduces the risk of depression among older adults (hazard ratio = 0.90; 95% confidence interval [0.83, 0.97]; p = .012). However, this effect diminishes and becomes negative as the intensity of caregiving increases.
CONCLUSION: Promoting intergenerational caregiving and managing caregiving intensity could enhance synergistic development between older adults and children while safeguarding older adults' mental health and well-being in later life.

paper.title: Treatment adherence and clinical response in adolescents with polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome.
paper.summary:
OBJECTIVES: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS) commonly manifests during adolescence and requires sustained treatment. This study aimed to evaluate treatment initiation, adherence, and clinical response to different therapeutic modalities in adolescents with PMOS.
METHODS: This observational study included 40 adolescents aged 14-18 years with PMOS who were evaluated and treated at a tertiary adolescent gynecology clinic. Medical records were retrospectively reviewed for baseline characteristics and recommended treatments, and a face-to-face questionnaire was used to assess treatment initiation, self-reported duration of uninterrupted adherence, and changes in clinical symptoms. Associations between treatment adherence, clinical response, and pediatric endocrinology consultation were evaluated.
RESULTS: Combined oral contraceptives (COCs) were the most frequently recommended treatment (75.0 %, n=30). Treatment initiation rates were 83.3 % (n=25) for COCs, 36.8 % (n=7) for weight loss interventions, 100 % (n=5) for progesterone therapy, 66.7 % (n=2) for metformin, and 42.9 % (n=3) for laser hair removal. While 20 % of participants (n=8) reported never initiating the recommended treatments, only 10 % (n=4) maintained uninterrupted treatment adherence for longer than 6 months. Regression of menstrual irregularities was reported more frequently among participants with adherence for at least 3 months than among those with shorter adherence (82.6 % vs. 52.9 %, p=0.043); corresponding rates for hirsutism regression were 54.5 % and 13.3 %, respectively (p=0.011). Pediatric endocrinology consultation was associated with adherence for at least 3 months (65.2 % vs. 23.5 %, p=0.009).
CONCLUSIONS: Long-term treatment adherence was low despite relatively high treatment initiation rates. Longer adherence was associated with greater reported improvement in menstrual irregularities and hirsutism. Multidisciplinary management may improve treatment adherence and clinical response in adolescents with PMOS.

paper.title: Harnessing lattice distortion for point-defect self-healing in multi-principal element alloys.
paper.summary: Multi-principal element alloys are promising structural materials for nuclear, aerospace, and fusion applications, yet their accelerated discovery is limited by the prohibitive cost of evaluating point-defect transport and self-healing behavior across vast compositional spaces. Here, we establish local lattice distortion (LLD), an intrinsic feature of chemically complex alloys, as a predictive and universal descriptor for vacancy-interstitial diffusivity convergence. We develop and validate a high-fidelity machine-learning interatomic potential based on the moment tensor potential formalism for body-centered-cubic Zr-Ti-Nb alloys, enabling accurate large-scale simulations of defect energetics and migration. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal a robust inverse correlation between LLD and the activation energy disparity between vacancies and interstitials. This relationship is further validated in face-centered-cubic V-Co-Ni and Ni-Pd systems, demonstrating transferability across distinct chemistries and crystal structures. LLD-induced narrowing of vacancy-interstitial mobility differences promotes Frenkel pair recombination and defect self-healing. Mechanistically, vacancy diffusion is governed by the energy barrier associated with bond-length compression at the saddle state, together with statistical sampling of low-barrier jumps mediated by oversized atoms. These findings establish lattice distortion as a powerful, physically grounded design lever that links nanoscale disorder to point-defect self-healing, offering a practical pathway for the accelerated discovery of next-generation structural materials for extreme environments.

paper.title: The debt burden of tropical cyclones and climate change.
paper.summary: Addressing climate change through mitigation and adaptation is expected to require more than $6 trillion in global investment annually by 2035. Yet many countries face significant barriers to accessing this finance, including low or absent credit ratings, large debt burdens, and high borrowing costs. Climate change may further amplify these barriers, creating a "vicious cycle" in which mounting economic losses reduce the capacity of countries to invest in adaptation and mitigation. We provide evidence that the cost and availability of capital for many countries have already been shaped by both historical exposure to naturally-occurring tropical cyclones (TCs) and anthropogenic warming. Our empirical estimates suggest that, on average across TC-exposed countries, 20% of debt-to-GDP ratios are attributable to TCs from 1980 to 2019. Across all countries, GDP levels are on average 12% lower due to the combined impacts of baseline naturally-occurring TCs and anthropogenic warming. In a separate correlational machine-learning analysis, we estimate that these macroeconomic impacts are associated with an increased likelihood of hotter countries receiving credit ratings below investment grade ([Formula: see text]BBB-), as well as persistent credit risk premiums of at least 1 basis point in 64 countries and 5 basis points in highly exposed countries. We provide estimates for 181 countries, including many TC-affected and/or hot countries that do not have bond yield data. Future increases in temperature and TC activity may further worsen sovereign credit conditions, potentially undermining climate resilience and long-run development prospects.

paper.title: The sound of persuasion: Using generative AI to identify gender gaps in political influence.
paper.summary: Women often experience a deficit in persuasive influence, particularly in contexts like politics, where expectations about women's behavior may conflict with gendered expectations about the domain and role. In spite of this widespread pattern, the mechanisms behind the gender gap in persuasion are difficult to isolate and test in dynamic political conversations. Women may be less persuasive simply because role-based expectations prompt others to afford women less authority when speaking about politics generally or about some political topics. Alternatively, women may be less persuasive because they tend to use linguistic patterns or rhetorical strategies that are less effective. Using an original AI-based approach, we put 4,300 human subjects into realistic, real-time phone conversations with an AI agent. These agents were randomly assigned either a masculine or feminine gendered conversation topic and a male- or female-sounding voice, allowing us to manipulate topic and perceptions of speakers' gender while holding constant other elements of rhetorical content and strategy. After validating the experimental treatments, we find no direct effects of perceived gender of the AI agent, as cued by voice. However, gender affects other important aspects of the persuasive interaction. Research subjects were more likely to be persuaded about the masculine topic (defense spending) than the feminine topic (aid to the poor). Additionally, women research subjects were, on average, more persuaded than men. To the extent that men and women emphasize different topics in political conversations and have different discussion partners, these dynamics are likely to shape women's political persuasive influence.

paper.title: Short-term flexibility and long-term stability in models of mind perception.
paper.summary: Understanding how people decide whether someone or something possesses a mind is central to a myriad of psychological, biological, and philosophical questions. It shapes fundamental processes at the individual (e.g., social interaction) and societal level (e.g., morality and ethics). While mind perception has been studied, it remains unclear which internal model people use when ascribing mental capacities to entities. Across four experiments (total N = 256), we explored what model people hold and its flexibility when ascribing agency and experience to entities encountered in everyday life and which differ in animacy and socialness (e.g., humans, pets, robots, voice assistants, tools). Using representational similarity analysis combined with lab-based experiments, a 6-wk long social interaction intervention, and longitudinal real-life exposure, we tested which model people use to ascribe agency and experience by comparing observed rating data to theoretical models. We demonstrated that an animacy distinction underlies the representational structure of experience attributions, while internal models for agency attributions are more idiosyncratic and flexible. When receiving explicit information on one entity, the internal model of agency changes. People update their model by incorporating this information, generalizing across the entire category of entities. We found no evidence that extended exposure to or ownership of inanimate technology, such as robots or voice assistants, or pets leads to restructuring of the models for experience or agency. Overall, these results provide insight into the internal models people hold when perceiving minds, the flexibility thereof, and offer ways to understand the roots and consequences of mind perception.

paper.title: A hybrid ultrafast phase transition in a chemically complex alloy under extreme conditions.
paper.summary: The face-centered cubic to hexagonal close-packed (FCC-HCP) phase transition is ubiquitous in static high-pressure experiments of conventional FCC metals and alloys, yet its conspicuous absence under laser shock compression (LSC) has remained a puzzle. Here we show that this transition can be realized and directly observed in the prototypical CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy alloy under LSC at pressures exceeding ~114 GPa and Hugoniot temperatures above ~1,800 K. Time-resolved X-ray diffraction reveals that the transformation occurs on a timescale at least as fast as 1 to 2 ns, orders of magnitude faster than diffusion-controlled nucleation-growth processes, yet reversible upon pressure release, unlike classical FCC-HCP martensitic transformations. We hypothesize that the high Hugoniot temperature may provide the atomic mobility for reversibility, while the extreme deviatoric stress likely promotes rapid, displacive atomic motion. This fusion of athermal speed and thermal reversibility is difficult to classify within the classical dichotomy of phase transitions as either purely martensitic or purely thermally activated and may represent a class of stress-assisted, thermally reversible transformation accessible only under extreme pressure-temperature (P-T) conditions. First-principles Gibbs free-energy calculations show that the HCP phase is thermodynamically favored at low temperature over the pressure range 50 to 142 GPa, and that the computed FCC-HCP phase boundary places the laser-shock P-T state on the HCP-stable side, making it accessible to the transient LSC path. Our findings are consistent with chemical complexity acting as a powerful parameter for controlling phase transformation pathways under extreme P-T conditions, and reveal a distinct class of ultrafast, reversible transformations.

paper.title: Evaluation of modern hematology-oncology home call: optimizing patient care, physician well-being, and trainee education.
paper.summary: Traditional home call, managing after-hours pager communications, remains a common component of hematology-oncology fellowship and modern practice. Little is known about these patient-related interactions and implications. The aim of this project was to characterize after-hours pager volumes and evaluate perceived impacts on care, physician well-being, and trainee education. We performed a mixed-methods study at a tertiary academic center, analyzing after-hours pager activity from 2020 to 2024 across hematology consult pagers (HCP), hematology outpatient pagers (HOP), and medical oncology pagers (MOP). A survey of hematology-oncology fellows evaluated perceptions and attitudes toward the home-call experience using free-text responses and a 5-point Likert scale. After-hours pager burden was substantial and sustained. The MOP received >3000 pages annually, with medians of 5 to 6 per weekday and 15 to 15.5 per weekend day. The HOP volume nearly doubled over the study period (960-1721 annually), with median pager volumes of 1 to 3 per weekday and 2 to 7 per weekend day. The HCP volume ranged from 594 to 768 pages annually. Survey response rate was 58% (19/33). Only 16% of fellows endorsed educational value from patient calls on MOP or HOP, and ≤5% agreed that call tasks required physician-level expertise. Respondents reported that the pager resulted in fatigue, anxiety, and social disruptions. Free-text responses revealed themes of low educational value, high nonurgent call volume, and system inefficiencies. Contemporary home call had substantial pager burdens with limited actionability, adverse effects on well-being, and low educational value. Systems engineering, including triage processes and augmented patient education, could help optimize patient care, physician well-being, and trainee education.

paper.title: Interjections and Emotion (with Special Reference to “Surprise” and “Disgust”)
paper.summary: “All languages have ‘emotive interjections’ (i.e., interjections expressing cognitively based feelings)” (Wierzbicka 1999, p. 276)—and yet emotion researchers have invested only a tiny research effort into interjections, as compared with the huge body of research into facial expressions and words for emotion categories. This article provides an overview of the functions, meanings, and cross-linguistic variability of interjections, concentrating on non-word-based ones such as Wow!, Yuck!, and Ugh! The aims are to introduce an area that will be unfamiliar to most readers, to illustrate how one leading linguistic approach (natural semantic metalanguage [NSM]) deals with interjectional meaning, and to start a discussion about an interdisciplinary research agenda for the study of emotive interjections. Examples are drawn from English, Polish, and Cantonese.

paper.title: The Mediating Role of Emotion Regulation Strategies in the Relationship Between Big Five Personality Traits and Anxiety and Depression Among Chinese Firefighters
paper.summary: Identification of protective factors to prevent firefighters' anxiety and depression is meaningful. We explored whether emotion-regulation strategies mediate the relationship between personality traits and anxiety and depression among Chinese firefighters. Approximately, 716 Chinese firefighters were recruited and completed the Emotion Regulation Questionnaire (ERQ), Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS), Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS), and Big Five Inventory−2 (BFI-2) Scale. Results (N = 622) indicated that only negative emotionality traits could predict anxiety symptoms. Meanwhile, the multilevel mediation effect analyses showed that conscientiousness through cognitive reappraisal could reduce anxiety and depression symptoms in Chinese firefighters. Our findings clarify Chinese firefighters' underlying emotion-regulation process between personality traits and anxiety and depression. Implications, limitations, and future directions are discussed.

paper.title: A Multimodal Emotion Perspective on Social Media Influencer Marketing: The Effectiveness of Influencer Emotions, Network Size, and Branding on Consumer Brand Engagement Using Facial Expression and Linguistic Analysis
paper.summary: Social media influencers rely on emotional connection to maintain and grow their followings and have value for brands. To date, however, no research has quantitatively examined the impact of emotion in the facial expressions and caption text that influencers use in their video posts on consumer engagement through likes, comments, and views of posts. Grounded in consumer brand engagement, psychological sense of community, and the behavior ecology view of facial displays, this study uses social media analytics, facial expression analysis, and computational linguistic analysis to assess the emotional substance of 402 video posts by prominent micro-, macro-, and mega-influencer mothers, known as InstaMoms, as exemplars of Instagram influencers. The study identifies that the amount of emotion used and specific discrete emotions have a meaningful influence on engagement, and both follower count and presence of branding saliently contribute to a more robust understanding of the relationship. Theoretical and practical implications are identified and discussed.

paper.title: Feeding Your Feelings: Emotion Regulation Strategies and Emotional Eating
paper.summary: The process by which emotions affect eating behavior emerges as one of the central unresolved questions in the field of emotional eating. The present studies address the hypothesis that the regulation strategies people use to deal with these emotions are responsible for increased eating. Negative emotions were induced and intake of comfort food and non—comfort food was measured by means of taste tests. Emotion induction was preceded by measuring individual differences in emotion regulation strategies (Study 1) or by instructions to regulate emotions in either an adaptive (reappraisal) or maladaptive (suppression) manner (Study 2). Study 3 also entailed a control condition without any regulation instructions. Relative to reappraisal and spontaneous expression, suppression led to increased food intake, but only of the comfort foods. Emotions themselves were not responsible for this effect. These findings provide new evidence that the way in which emotions are regulated affects eating behavior.

paper.title: The Interplay of Context, Experience, and Emotion at World Heritage Sites: a Qualitative and Machine Learning Approach
paper.summary:
This study illustrates how user-generated content, posted in the form of heritage site reviews on social media, can serve to reveal the relationship between the cocreated interpretation of World Heritage Sites (WHSs)—in terms of values, tangible and intangible attributes, as well
 as site visit logistics—and the emotional experience of the site. Two WHSs are taken as a case study. More than 2,000 reviews were retrieved from TripAdvisor and analyzed through the application of a mixed method that integrates qualitative digital ethnography and machine learning. Results
 show that TripAdvisor reviews capture tourists' emotional reactions from personal encounters with heritage and provide insights into the range of values—including the social, historic, and aesthetical values—that visitors experience when engaging with aspects of the past to associate
 meanings for the present. Results also show that the relation between experiences gained at WHSs and contextual aspects is not linear; instead, it is a complex one that results from the interaction of different factors and their associated sentiments. We discuss our results by reflecting on
 their theoretical and practical implications.

paper.title: Bridging supportive communication and interpersonal emotion regulation: An integrative review
paper.summary:
Social interactions that support people who are experiencing negative emotions are ubiquitous in a wide array of interpersonal relationships. These social interactions are referred to as
                    supportive communication
                    . Decades ago, Burleson and Goldsmith (1998) first noted a connection between supportive communication and emotion regulation, with the goal of explaining the underlying mechanisms by which supportive messages change the recipient’s negative emotions. Since then, contemporary emotion regulation theory has matured, and now can explain a broad range of supportive communication processes via the expansion of interpersonal emotion regulation research and the development of the process model of emotion regulation. This paper aims to describe how contemporary advances in emotion regulation theory and research can shed light on dynamic processes in supportive communication. We then discuss the implications of this updated view for both research fields and show how it can advance interdisciplinary research.
